name: Abraham Lincoln
hook: The president Jeopardy asks about more than any other — from a Kentucky log cabin to Ford's Theatre.

facts.label: 16th president
facts.statement: Lincoln was the 16th president, elected in 1860 and re-elected in 1864; Karl Marx called him "the single-minded son of the working class."

facts.label: Stephen Douglas
facts.statement: Lincoln lost an 1858 Senate race to Stephen Douglas, then beat him in the 1860 presidential election.

facts.label: Kentucky
facts.statement: He was born in a log cabin in Kentucky in 1809, near what is now Hodgenville.

facts.label: Gettysburg Address
facts.statement: He delivered the Gettysburg Address on November 19, 1863; it lasted about two minutes and begins "Four score and seven years ago."
associations: Four score and seven years ago

facts.label: Emancipation Proclamation
facts.statement: The Emancipation Proclamation took effect January 1, 1863; Lincoln called it "a fit and necessary war measure."

facts.label: Andrew Johnson
facts.statement: Lincoln chose Democrat Andrew Johnson as his 1864 running mate; Johnson became president after the assassination.

facts.label: George McClellan
facts.statement: McClellan was the "Young Napoleon of the West" before Lincoln sacked him; then McClellan ran against Lincoln in 1864.
